I hit the character limit for this review so I will write more on the comments. TL;DR version: Cool game, its just fun to fight multitude of orcs and the personality\diversity of captains will keep you entertained.
I am not a LOTR fan, read the first book and stopped in the middle of the second due to having so many characters and couldnt remember who was who. Eventually watched the movie and liked, but still not really a huge thing to me as it is to some people.
The game has some classic characters from the series, and I think they fit the story well. But after all said and done, I wasnt really impressed with it, and after two lame battles with quick time events, the ending left me confused since it didnt answer my question, and was a cliffhanger.
The voice acting of the characters in the story is good, but they really excel as you listen to the random orc banter in game, they are very varied and fun, the writers and voice actors did a great job in making them interesting.
I am going to separate this part in multiple sections.
First of all, if you want a challenge, disable
Runes DLC that you may have gotten, they are really overpowered. Granting a chance of avoiding a fatal blow, increasing slow-motion time when aiming with a bow or doing extra damage when you have a hit-streak can help a lot in the beginning, theres even one that makes the character immune to poison, eliminating a game mechanic right from start. Another one that grants those unbalanced runes is the free Defiance DLC, but it also includes a game trial mode and a new character skin. So just avoid using those runes and earn your own.
Most of the game you fight Uruks and it starts off frighteningly simple and easy, you just have a attack and parry button and use them all the time. When a ranged enemy attacks, you do a roll (which I fail to do often, and the vast majority of my deaths were due to ranged captains who have an attack that removes 70% of your health striking me as I was focused on the enemies nearby). Eventually the captains you find with certain invulnerabilities and new kinds of soldiers that appear some time later will require a little more diversity in your moves.
One of the interesting points in the game is the amount of foes you will face at the same time. As you battle with a small group of orcs, the ones nearby will investigate the noise and join the fray. If you invade a fortress and let them sound the alarm, be ready to fight 30 or more enemies and more will keep coming. At the beginning this will be a little difficult and time consuming, but as you unlock skills it becomes easier since they allow you defeat multiple foes in a short amount of time.
Talking about special skills, one you acquire later in the game allows you to
The much talked about Nemesis system, is where random uruks assigned to be captains and warchiefs, the game equivalent of bosses, rise and fall in strength and rank due to your action or inaction.
They all have different faces, strengths, weakness, armor (that improves as they raise in rank) and personality. There are more than 20 of them spread around the map and you will constantly find them even if you arent looking for it. Its very common for you to fight a random group of orcs, and they randomly appear and greet you before a fight. You can even be hunting for a specific captain, and in the middle of combat one or two more show up to make things harder.
They can also be only available to fight in specific missions. When they are recruiting orcs, having a feast, battling a beast to prove his worth or fight another captain he isnt fond of. You can interrupt those events or just watch them unfold, with them gaining strength if they succeed.
Some are bodyguards of the Warchiefs, the top bosses who answer to Sauron, who will only appear when special conditions are met, such as making a orc he is fond of squeal, or killing multiple followers with fire to get his attention.
The lines of captains and warchiefs can be menacing, sophisticated or just plain crazy, and they all have unique speech for each situation. They can remember if you run away from them calling you a coward, or if they ran from you, for a strategic retreat. They comment if you are surrounded by enemies, sneaked around to attack him or if you kept "killing" them but they came back (one captain I killed 3 times, the last fight removing his head. But he later appeared with a mask, swearing vengeance... surprising and amusing me to no end).
They all have strengths and weakness that you should pay attention to, specially at high levels. You can find a captain\warchief who is afraid of nearly everything and make him a easy target exploiting his weakness, as a example by burning him, or insta-killing him with a stealth or ranged attack, or fight against one who is a warmaster with fire weapon and do a devastating grab attack and have a sequence of blows that you must parry each, coupled with invulnerability of stun or regular strikes. They can become stronger if you enrage them. One of the possibilities is a hate for a beast called Caragor, if you bring one to battle (or they accidentally appear), you will make him angry and stronger.
They are a great addition to the game. In one case I fought a captain, almost beat him but he got enraged for "fear of losing" but  immediately started to run because a captain he dislikes appeared soon afterwards, triggering his "fear of rival". You can get a lot of unique situations that you cant predict due to this.
Remember the special skill I mentioned before? With it you can
Stealth is another part of the game. Even if you dislike this, fret not. The ones that are essential to missions are rare and quite easy if you dont aim for the extra objectives. I found it to be a good way of dispatching Orcs in fortresses, but if you just prefer to go
swords blazing, thats completely doable. The optional stealth missions can be a little challenging for people who arent used to sneaking around, but I find them to be fun and forgiving on the difficulty scale.
The game have some challenges (trials) and two expansions. The challenges are interesting but unfortunately they give a bonus if you are fast enough, and I hate fighting against the clock, so I didnt have much fun trying to hurry up and kill the captains and warchiefs as quickly as I could. My brief review of the expansions will be from memory of 3 years ago so I wont give much details on it, sorry. Look for them in the comments.
Overall this is just a fun game to play, and if you are a LOTR fan it will probably be even better. Like all games it will be repetitive, specially if you aim for doing everything available on it, but you dont care because you are just mowing down orcs and having fun finding the weakpoints of the captains\warchiefs. The expansions are nice but not something to write home about.
Seriously, get this game!

First, it is a fun game. I will get that statement out of the way.
I find that concept of nature being the most viscious enemy to be really clever, your worst dangers can vary based on your position; if you're over the ocean, sharks are your main concern as they will attack your boat, pushing you into the water in an attempt to turn you into their next meal, after the hunters of the deep you'll find drowning to be your second biggest danger because you will need to find supplies and the fastest way to get them is from sunken ships but you can't stay down there forever. While on land, the danger often comes from simpler things such as a lack of clean water or regular food supply (though they recently added fish traps to make it a little easier).
Some helpful tips for beginners:
Right now, food doesn't spoil so if you see crabs you can kill them and gather tham at your camp, cook them as you like (never eat raw)
Buckets may seem useless but once you find one, empty it of any sea water and then leave it standing up, it will catch rain and act as a regular source of drinking water, make sure to gather as many of these as you can (2 to 4 is a good starting number), they can be used to refill water bottles for portable water sources
Do not settle on the first island you find, make note of the space, the trees, the yucca plants and stones, if you don't have enough and other islands are far, gather a few supplies and move, your best island is one not too far from others with plenty of supplies (at least when you start off)
This is survival in its simplest form, this isn't like Don't Starve where enemies may show up if you burn down trees or random dogs might attack, this game can be both simple and frustrating.

I will admit that I haven't been following the series the whole time, but I've played Dynasty Warriors 3 and a little of 4, 5, and 7. I did not like 7, and my hopes weren't very high for this game, but let me tell you...awesome!!!
Pros:
Brought back correct weapons - I remember in 7 that Xiahou Dun had a two handed mace, where as every other one he had a scimitar. He has the scimitar again! And other fixes like that.
Long Campaign mode - you play by faction, not by character, which I like because you get to try out different characters and the story is much longer and it doesn't get as repetitive. Each level gives you 2-4 characters to pick from.
Weapon Customization - while it may be a little cheap, every character has 2 weapons that they can switch between in battle. Some weapons are more compatible with the warrior than others (rated 1-4 stars). So even if you find a weapon that you really like, it doesn't make sense for ALL of your characters to use that weapon. And every warrior has a specialty weapon that they are supposed to use, but you can change it.
Cons:
Graphics - there is nothing really special about the graphics, and I see some graphical flaws here and there (lines across the face, etc.) but it doesn't stop me from playing.
Plot holes - I remember fighting Zhang He in one battle and the next level he was on my side. What happened? Why is he my friend now?
Other usual bugs - I killed Diao Chan. Lu Bu got angry. The English message said "Diao Chan is enraged at Lu Bu's death" (something along those lines)
Controls - the default controls for the Xbox Controller are my biggest problem. I had to remap them completely because none of it made any sense. And I HATE that the musou button and OK button are the same mapping, because I use B for musou and OK should be A, so now whenever I want to confirm something it's B, and cancel is A...
Overall -
I can get used to the controls, though they are annoying. Everything else is not a dealbreaker to me. I've already put 8 hours into the Wei campaign and I love it.

Hylics is a hidden gem, and from the screenshots alone anyone can see it looks utterly unique- it's a crazy trip. A lot of the reviews talk about that aspect and the insane, randomly generated writing, so I'll focus on how it plays. Hylics was quite a bit deeper than I expected in terms of mechanics and what it offers up.
Combat at the start feels pretty meh when you're a one-man team, but even so smart use of the moves at your disposal makes combat interesting and as you start finding companions (they're all missable!) and learning more moves you get a pretty interesting combination of tactics! Battles are a rather standard affair otherwise, being turn-based. However there's no random battles, and enemies stay dead once defeated- they literally turn into a mushy pool of blood and bones on the map forever. And of course the animations of attacks are a pleasure to see and your foes have... interesting aesthetics, to say the least, so it offsets some of the monotony. At the end of each battle, you'll get Meat for the enemies you slayed.
Adding onto to that, death works differently here. Instead of the usual game over, you're put into a kind of hub only accessible by death. The Meat you found can be grinded to increase your HP- since there's no leveling up, at least not visibly as far as I know- so if you've saved some up the same enemy that killed you may not be so tough next time. I ended up here a lot at the beginning. I really enjoyed this, it's very different from pretty much any other RPG Maker game.
It's also fairly non-linear. There's the main path, of course, but hidden NPCs, companions, and items encourage exploration which is fun thanks to the fact that there aren't random battles. Usually, those discourage me from exploring freely.
So if you're a fan of RPG Maker games, or unique aesthetics and writing, this is for you. But it's also just a really solid game, and I'm surprised it has as much as it does. You can play through and disregard the bells and whistles and you'll still have fun, but for completionists or those who want an excuse to soak up more of Mason Lindroth's acid-fueled world, it's a good time.

The quests were boring. Of the quests I did so far in my time playing there were fetch quests and "go to a point, maybe kill a thing" quests. They were also very linear. One quest involved
The graphics are where this game succeeds the most. They're not crazy, out of this world graphics, but they are quite charming and give a good aesthetic to the world.

I feel as though this game fills a void many sandbox games are missing nowadays, I feel like if you enjoy games like terraria, or starbound, you will see this game has a new...."perspective" on the genre, but i digress, I absolutely love the story element to the game in single player, and i firmly believe the game has alot of potential. Overall i think the control scheme is difficult to get used to, but the overall theme and design of the aesthetic makes up for me in a lot of ways. If you want something new to sink your teeth into and have a profound love for sandbox games, this ones going to scratch that itch for little while.

-The characters are cute and charming (remind me of Gomez's people from Fez)
-The building is simple and makes sense, so it's easy to build a nice sized home and expand on it.
-The combat is engaging, though there are only a few types of weaponry at the moment between spells, Sword/shield and a Bow it is still fun and each weapon presents it's own challenge of mastering.
-Enemies are fairly unique, and each react and fight differently making you learn several combat styles for dealing with them.
-Boss fights are fun and challenging, so dying a few times before you completely learn the fight is expected, but the cost of death is very forgiving, just a bit of exp loss so it's not a big deal and still feels great to drop a big baddie.
-The game is very fleshed out for an EA title and playing for just a couple of hours each day leaves plenty left to come back to and work on, giving this title a good long lifespan to look forward to, especially as they add more content and quality of life features.
-A few things I think it could really use:
-Better warping technology, such as placing multiple pads and allowing you to select which one to warp if you have multiple bases.
-a Mini Map would be appreciated as getting chased by enemies while at low life then needing to stop to open up your map to see that you ran past your base 15 seconds ago to then have to run back cause you traverse land faster than you realize.
-Displaying your armor, or at least your hat would be a nice touch.
Overall I highly recommend this game, it's very affordable; a lot of fun; has great features; is easy going and runs well on lower end machines if that's your concern.

[Note] Hear me out, there's a damn good reason this review is so long even though I don't recommend it. Like, I'm not just hating on it for no reason.
Despite the fact that steam says I've only played 27 minutes, I have played more as I was without internet for a little while and logged a decent amount of playtime then, however it didn't seem to log the time in steam. Anyways, on with the review.
Let me just start off by saying that I don't 'hate' this game, but seriously don't even bother wasting your time with it. It's fairly cheap, sure, but even that doesn't justify buying the game. Oh, and hear me out before giving this a thumbs down, like I said I don't hate the game, but I'm trying to be objective here.
The menus are a bit clunky, not exactly difficult to navigate or anything like that, just lacks certain... ease of use functionalities that I've grown acustomed to with better designed games. Of course I understand "Small indie studio, Early access, don't expect it to be perfect blah blah blah" but regardless of whatever excuses or justification, it doesn't change the fact that it does make the game that much more difficult to enjoy. This includes inventory management, crafting, storage, hotbar, using/binding skills & equipment, etc.
Movement is a little messed up. The game is setup in an isometric sort of style, but the character doesn't move along the same axis as the world, which makes it really annoying to try and follow a path or navigate the world. Mind you, it's not 'that' far off, but it's off enough where you'll absolutely notice it, and if you're a stickler for game-feel like me, it will drive you mad.
Combat; Before I say anything, I just want to clarify again, I don't 'hate' this game, but I'm just gonna go off in a little rant here. The combat in this game is about as satisfying as a fleshlight lined with sandpaper; It only feels good if you're part of the really niche audience that somehow enjoys that, or if you have no clue what a normal fleshlight feels like. So the combat 'works', but the hitbox is sort of glitchy, or so it would seem. There have been times where I had tried to slash at an enemy, but after the enemy moved in closer, it would be "outside" of my sword range, despite literally standing on my toes. Now perhaps this is an issue only I've experienced, I don't know, but I think it's definitely worth mention. Never tried Ranged combat or Magic because I just didn't have the patience to get that far.
Basebuilding is kinda goofy. For instance, I was able to build a floor, door, chest, workbench, roof, windows, a garden, and an alchemy table, all before I was able to build walls. Yup, spent most of my time playing without walls, but thank god I had an alchemy table right? Not to mention learn telepathy to hold my roof up. Boy oh boy, I knew how to levitate a giant wooden roof and brew complex potions before I knew how stack wood. Plus the floor/roof tiles are pretty large, which, in my opinion makes the building system pretty boring and leaves very little to creative freedom. But that's neither here nor there. Not to mention when trying to place something that has multiple variants (colors, different placement angles, etc.) you just had to scroll with no indication of what's coming up or what you've already past, just a number. Again, neither here nor there, but just another small thing that makes this game 'that' much more difficult to enjoy.
One of the last points is the games difficulty. Mind you, I'm not saying the game is "difficult" per se, but it feels like it's half-in/half-out of the pool of hardcore survival. In general this game seems/seemed like it was going to be a pretty light/casual open-world survival game, however with small inventory stacks (10 per stackable item), and relatively scarce resources (scarce in terms of how much you need versus how easy it is to gather quickly), it makes the game feel as though it's trying for more of a hardcore survival feel. Now before anyone says, "UGH It's not that hard to gather resources you just suck!" I know, I agree with that first part, it's not particularly difficult to gather resources, but at the same time when I have to spend an entire (in-game) day gathering grass just so I can fill my hunger bar or gather marshmallows to refill my HP, that's a little rediculous. Regardless very early on I figured out it's much easier to just let my character die and respawn than to actually keep myself fed or healed, and that's not a good thing for any player to decide for any game. And again, "Early access blah blah" doesn't change the fact of what the game is right now and whether or not I would recommend it right now, which I wouldn't.
On a brighter note, I do think the artstyle is pretty cute. The game itself is aesthetically pleasing, with a consistent art-style and nice colors. Not to mention the soundtrack is pretty good too. So kudos to the art and music designers. Unfortunately those are the only commendations that come to mind.
TLDR; On a scale from 0-10 where a 7 = buy the game, this game is a solid 6 and a half. Generally not a particularly enjoyable game, but it's not horrible, it's cheap, and it looks nice and has 7.8/10 music.
One way I would put it; In an age where so many indie developers intentionally release ♥♥♥♥♥♥ games to scam money out of people, these developers don't seem villainous, just inexperienced, and not even terribly so, just a little bit.

Oh wow, Mass Effect. Where to begin?
It's the game that started the franchise. I really love this game. Long before I bought it on Steam I had already beaten it on Xbox. This is a game that means a lot to me. It truly showed me the storytelling potential of an RPG. I absolutely love the decision-making mechanics. The gameplay was equally awesome. I challenge you to show me a game that can make an equally logical case for infinite ammo as ME1 did.
And that's really what it comes down to. ME1 is just so logical. Sure, it is sci-fi, but it's sci-fi that makes sense. With just some slight suspension of disbelief, everything in the game COULD be true. And that's also the real tragedy of the game. ME2 was also pretty great, but really let's pretend the game just ended there and we can all forget about ME3 and ME:A.

Mass Effect... where to start?
I suppose the first thing one needs to say when talking about Mass Effect is that there are a trilogy of games, and you need to judge them as such. It is not a series which you can jump into half way through and expect to get the full potential of it. Similarly, Mass Effect requires a bit of an investment from the player in terms of time and emotion - if you are someone who will merrily skip through every cutscene and jump straight from mission to mission without any interest in taking the time to explore the ship and the universe, then you will probably find Mass Effect to be a something average cover-shooter.
With that out of the way, if you DO put a bit of time and investment into the game, it is an emotional rollercoaster and one of the best modern RPGs out there. The voice acting and the characters are what really set it apart from the crowd - every companion in each of the three games has their own story, some with triumphant and happy endings, others... less so. This is coupled with a fantastic musical score throughout the trilogy, adding that extra bit of gravitas and tension when needed - this is one of the very few games where I have gone out and bought the soundtrack, and simply hearing a couple of the songs (such as 'Leaving Earth') to-date sends shivers down my spine.
Regarding the first Mass Effect, which this review is supposed to be for, it is arguably the weakest of the trilogy, due to its age as much as anything. The story is still very solid, if a bit clichéd at times, but the overall feel of the universe is a bit more stale than in the successors. The combat is good, although perhaps a little dated compared with newer games. Ultimately, the first game is all about setting the scene and introducing/building a lot of the key characters who will recur throughout the series. Some elements, such as the planet exploration, can get a bit repetitive, but to be honest these can mostly be skipped at this point - as long as you are following the main story and interacting with most of the characters you will be fine.
In terms of the overall trilogy, remember that a lot of your decisions will carry over to the next game(s), so the more time you invest in some of the 'side quests' the better. Even innocuous seeming decisions can have a habit of rearing their heads much later down the line in the story. The game remembering that you punched that annoying news reporter and referencing it in ME3 is the sort of nice little touch which makes it worth considering your actions.
I could go on for pages but would be mostly repeating myself - the bottom line is that Mass Effect is one of those games where it just say "Trust me, things are going to get really good" - and if you do, they will. I envy those who havent yet played through these games, and havent experienced the twists and turns, and some of the most heart-wrenching moments I have ever witnessed in a computer game.

State of Decay is a great game. There is a great, open-world to explore, a church to upgrade, and yes, plenty of zombies to kill.  However, there are a few issues in the game, primarily the frame rate and zombie teleporting. The frame rate drops out of nowhere, stooping to rates of 5-10, though only for a second (long enough for you to get your neck chewed off).  Also, zombies to teleport and respawn almost instantainously, without your realizing. One for instance, popped right in front of me when I was barricaiding a room. Finally for the issues, there is perma-death.  That means, when you dead, YOU DEAD!!! But, none of these minor problems should stop you from playing one of the best zombie games in history.  Combat is fluid, and the ground take-downs are sick.  The amount of blood and gore also makes each swing of a spiked bat murderous and powerful.  Probably one of the game's highest strong points is the sound.  Each moan of a zombie and the shuffiling of the footsteps make your heart skip a beat and wonder where the heck that one (or two, or three) zombie is at.  All and all, State of Decay is an amazing game and an even better zombie survival RPG, witch shouldn't be passed up because of a few minor bugs.

A tale of two sisters indeed, Chant and Elise are very close.  One was turned into a fairy because neither one had a sense of restraint against jewels, and so they go to find a way to turn her back.  Then they find out that it's a huge cycle that some evil overlord plays out repeatedly, and that in order to seal him away they have to use up all of the fairy-sister's fairy dust - which will in turn kill her.
The gameplay in this is really good, even given the linear environment - the combat system plays like a cross between Legend of Zelda and Monster Hunter.  Each zone in each stage has a bonus item you can get by doing a specific action (you WILL want to use a walkthrough for this, otherwise you'll have very little help in figuring it out), and the spell system is just simplistic enough to get familiar with it fairly quickly.  The story turns dark halfway through, but the ending makes up for it handily (until the last few sentences, which pretty much shoot your closure in the face).
Simple, colorful, fun and playable.  Give it a shot if it's in your budget.

I hit the character limit for this review so I will write more on the comments. TL;DR version: Cool game, its just fun to fight multitude of orcs and the personality\diversity of captains will keep you entertained.
I am not a LOTR fan, read the first book and stopped in the middle of the second due to having so many characters and couldnt remember who was who. Eventually watched the movie and liked, but still not really a huge thing to me as it is to some people.
The game has some classic characters from the series, and I think they fit the story well. But after all said and done, I wasnt really impressed with it, and after two lame battles with quick time events, the ending left me confused since it didnt answer my question, and was a cliffhanger.
The voice acting of the characters in the story is good, but they really excel as you listen to the random orc banter in game, they are very varied and fun, the writers and voice actors did a great job in making them interesting.
I am going to separate this part in multiple sections.
First of all, if you want a challenge, disable
Runes DLC that you may have gotten, they are really overpowered. Granting a chance of avoiding a fatal blow, increasing slow-motion time when aiming with a bow or doing extra damage when you have a hit-streak can help a lot in the beginning, theres even one that makes the character immune to poison, eliminating a game mechanic right from start. Another one that grants those unbalanced runes is the free Defiance DLC, but it also includes a game trial mode and a new character skin. So just avoid using those runes and earn your own.
Most of the game you fight Uruks and it starts off frighteningly simple and easy, you just have a attack and parry button and use them all the time. When a ranged enemy attacks, you do a roll (which I fail to do often, and the vast majority of my deaths were due to ranged captains who have an attack that removes 70% of your health striking me as I was focused on the enemies nearby). Eventually the captains you find with certain invulnerabilities and new kinds of soldiers that appear some time later will require a little more diversity in your moves.
One of the interesting points in the game is the amount of foes you will face at the same time. As you battle with a small group of orcs, the ones nearby will investigate the noise and join the fray. If you invade a fortress and let them sound the alarm, be ready to fight 30 or more enemies and more will keep coming. At the beginning this will be a little difficult and time consuming, but as you unlock skills it becomes easier since they allow you defeat multiple foes in a short amount of time.
Talking about special skills, one you acquire later in the game allows you to
The much talked about Nemesis system, is where random uruks assigned to be captains and warchiefs, the game equivalent of bosses, rise and fall in strength and rank due to your action or inaction.
They all have different faces, strengths, weakness, armor (that improves as they raise in rank) and personality. There are more than 20 of them spread around the map and you will constantly find them even if you arent looking for it. Its very common for you to fight a random group of orcs, and they randomly appear and greet you before a fight. You can even be hunting for a specific captain, and in the middle of combat one or two more show up to make things harder.
They can also be only available to fight in specific missions. When they are recruiting orcs, having a feast, battling a beast to prove his worth or fight another captain he isnt fond of. You can interrupt those events or just watch them unfold, with them gaining strength if they succeed.
Some are bodyguards of the Warchiefs, the top bosses who answer to Sauron, who will only appear when special conditions are met, such as making a orc he is fond of squeal, or killing multiple followers with fire to get his attention.
The lines of captains and warchiefs can be menacing, sophisticated or just plain crazy, and they all have unique speech for each situation. They can remember if you run away from them calling you a coward, or if they ran from you, for a strategic retreat. They comment if you are surrounded by enemies, sneaked around to attack him or if you kept "killing" them but they came back (one captain I killed 3 times, the last fight removing his head. But he later appeared with a mask, swearing vengeance... surprising and amusing me to no end).
They all have strengths and weakness that you should pay attention to, specially at high levels. You can find a captain\warchief who is afraid of nearly everything and make him a easy target exploiting his weakness, as a example by burning him, or insta-killing him with a stealth or ranged attack, or fight against one who is a warmaster with fire weapon and do a devastating grab attack and have a sequence of blows that you must parry each, coupled with invulnerability of stun or regular strikes. They can become stronger if you enrage them. One of the possibilities is a hate for a beast called Caragor, if you bring one to battle (or they accidentally appear), you will make him angry and stronger.
They are a great addition to the game. In one case I fought a captain, almost beat him but he got enraged for "fear of losing" but  immediately started to run because a captain he dislikes appeared soon afterwards, triggering his "fear of rival". You can get a lot of unique situations that you cant predict due to this.
Remember the special skill I mentioned before? With it you can
Stealth is another part of the game. Even if you dislike this, fret not. The ones that are essential to missions are rare and quite easy if you dont aim for the extra objectives. I found it to be a good way of dispatching Orcs in fortresses, but if you just prefer to go
swords blazing, thats completely doable. The optional stealth missions can be a little challenging for people who arent used to sneaking around, but I find them to be fun and forgiving on the difficulty scale.
The game have some challenges (trials) and two expansions. The challenges are interesting but unfortunately they give a bonus if you are fast enough, and I hate fighting against the clock, so I didnt have much fun trying to hurry up and kill the captains and warchiefs as quickly as I could. My brief review of the expansions will be from memory of 3 years ago so I wont give much details on it, sorry. Look for them in the comments.
Overall this is just a fun game to play, and if you are a LOTR fan it will probably be even better. Like all games it will be repetitive, specially if you aim for doing everything available on it, but you dont care because you are just mowing down orcs and having fun finding the weakpoints of the captains\warchiefs. The expansions are nice but not something to write home about.
Seriously, get this game!

First at all, what is Shadow of Mordor? Its great Uruk killing Simulator. You can kill uruks in so many ways, so many of them, and in so cinematic way, that killing uruks become a main game. Lets get this straight, i'm a Homestuck fan and many who bought this game are too. This is my first review so go easy on me. As a fan Hiveswap exceeded all my expectations, but for the sake of the review i'm putting all my Homestuck love aside.
The story: On its own the story is funny and interesting, it gives you a sense of wonder in all its jokes and dialogue. The first half of the game is very captivating in the interactions with the environment ranging from Bubsy posters to monsters chasing you around the house. It really makes you feel like there's more to this world that we think. The second half the protagonist is swapped to another planet where you get to take control of (spoilers) Xefros the troll. During this time you really get to know and understand the "universe" Andrew Hussie has in store for us, you get to see its problems and its MiRaClEs. It shows us just how different but not different the "trolls" really are. Too bad it just builds us up to the real story that'll come out in the next acts.
The characters: The game starts us off with the siblings Joey Claire and Jude Harley taking control of Joey most of the time. In the first area of the game you get to learn about Joey and her point of view of environment. Each dialogue inteaction is from Joey's mind on the subject like how she wants to be a veterinarian to oppose her negective father. Have you ever done something as a counter to someone close. Jude likes to make conspiracy theories, do you like finding out answers to something or predicting the answer. Xefros is a chill dude who likes sports and music but is constanty terrorized by his red blood color which basicly makes you low class. Do you like sports but are discouraged by something you can't contol, these characters are relatable in a way good way. It immerses deeper into why we love video games and entertainment in general to begin with. It lets us feel like we can do things that are impossible.
The gameplay: I personally don't like to read books but hiveswap does in a way that makes me clicking for more. There are SO SO many hilarious jokes that it doesn't feel that taxing to be reading multiple lines. Combined with the great characters the jokes add to the level of interest within the dialogue. All of the places you explore are well drawn and cartoony and it feels like Homestuck at its core, but still different enough for somebody who's never seen Homestuck to enjoy it just as much as the next guy. On the puzzle side it's a little meak but fun nonetheless, it's definitely not as hard as other point and click adventure games. It is a little heavy on the reading side, for example there's a part where you read dialogue from a pad, it becomes slow at times thinking I just want to skip this to get to the rest of the game. The Characters and jokes really save it when it comes to this, anyone who fully reads all the dialogue will enjoy the game more, making you want to find more. That is for me at least.
MiRaClEs: This is what made Homestuck so popular in the first place. Relatable characters, funny dialogue, and exciting lore. Have you ever wished you could play sburb, or fight monsters, or save a princess. Thats what it means to really play Hive swap, it has a nice balance of relatability and fantasy. So if you like games but LOVE Homestuck I absolutely recommend this game.
- Anyway sorry if there's some grammer mistakes or I mispell something, it's my first time trying this but if you read this far THANK YOU go read Homestuck and buy Hiveswap (HeHe). <3

I used to play this game for hours on console, and now playing it on PC, it's still so easy to see why I fell in love with this game. First, here's pros/cons:
Pros:
+ Unique battle system (reminiscent of Shadow of the Colossus at times, hack & slash RPG at other times)
+ Variety of classes/skills for custom builds
+ Spells in the game look & feel AMAZING when you're using them
+ Character customization (not only can you customize your own character, but you can also customize your companion).
+ Solid voice acting (*see cons list for 2 comments on this)
+ Environments look pretty good (it's a screenshot-worthy game at times)
+ Enemy variety is much better than most RPGs
+ Great replay value (end-game changes in NG+)
+ DLC that can be extremely hard, depending on your skill/character levels. Provides a good reason to keep leveling.
+ Small choices in the game can lead to consequences down the road (i.e. You can keep (or pay an NPC to dupe) items instead of turning in quests, but if that item is missing/magical (NPC dupes don't have magical properties), then certain cutscenes can trigger where if a character has that quest item, you'd save a ton of time/get special items.
Neutral:
Character models are really hit and miss. Some look great, others are pretty bad (when talking/showing emotions)
Soundtrack, for me, is also hit or miss. Some tracks are A+, others are forgettable.
Some dungeons feel like they go on ENTIRELY too long. (These past two points are subjective, I know)
The fast travel system is complete bull-crap at times. Other times it's not half bad. All in all, I put this in neutral.
A lot of quests can be completely skipped, especially if you don't go hunting for them at weird times. Without these, some characters just disappear and you don't know why, or show up in weird places without a backstory.
Cons:
- *A ton of lines for your companions (you make one & choose two others, for a party of 4) are all recycled entirely too much. I'm talking like "I'm sworn to carry your burdens"-level. (
)
- *One or two characters were supposed to have an accent, and you can tell that the VA forced it. It's not immersion-breaking, but whoever did QC on it shouldn't have let it pass.
- The game is no stranger to the idea of re-using story dungeons for side quests.
- The game uses a point-based romance system to decide who you "end up with" at the end (unless you acquire a certain item through a side quest). Not being careful toward the end of the game can make your character end up with a certain NPC who gives you a metric ton of quests 2/3 of the way through the game, as completing quests gives huge point boosts.
- While the story is fantastic, the writing toward the end is slightly melodramatic and convoluted. The payout is totally worth it, I just think it could use some touch-ups or maybe make a few silent scenes better animated to match their emotions.
- There's a gifting system that does literally nothing, unless you give the same character 40 billion copies of the same thing, and even then the impact is so small that if you just so much as un-sheath your weapon in front of them, those 40 billion copies are negated.
- It suffers from a Skyrim complex (i.e. "Oh, I'm dying." *Opens up menu and consumes 5 health items*). Some like this style, but I prefer there to at least be some sort of potion-drinking animation so I at least don't feel like 54 cheese wheels can resurrect the almost-dead.
-------------
Overall, I give the game a solid 8.5/10.
-------------
It's definitely not perfect, but it's a lot better than most RPG games out there. Not only can you climb enemies, but many bosses are so much larger-than-life, that you'll need to if you want to have any hope of defeating them.
If you want to play a ranged/magic-based character, this game is fantastic for that, too. You can even combine them and use a magic archer, who summons arrows out of thin air. Not a lot of games allow that. And when it comes to spells, summoning a lightning bolt and using it as whip, or even summoning a tornado--the visual effects on spells in this game are stunning and very well animated.
The story-line often takes work to find, as a lot of quests are buried or only available during a very short time (one character's personal quest is unavailable until you complete one main quest mission, and is then unavailable after you accept the very next main quest mission. Meaning if you don't turn the first quest in, leave, and find the NPC, the quest is just GONE. And considering how important that quest is to knowing why in the world she can just show up later, it can be pretty confusing if you don't play it.)
But when you DO find the story, it's very well written and quite compelling. There are a few animated cutscenes that aren't the most polished, but for a game that came out when it did, and how much customization there is, I can't really complain, especially when the environment looks like it does. This game aims for "gritty, dark fantasy" at times, and "magical, high-fantasy" at other times, and it's always right on the nose.
Again, 8.5/10. It's not perfect, but it's far better than others give it credit for. I consider this the hidden gem of 2012. While others were still exploring Skyrim, I was playing this, and I don't regret it.

If you like companions constantly spouting nonsense while going on a grand adventure filled with fighting monsters and being confused at the plot of a story, you're in the right place. Modding is literally the only reason I'd ever suggest getting this for the PC, it really is just a slapped onto PC port. Is it bad? No, not at all. It's not for everyone, I'd even say you should probably look at more serious reviews before you buy it, but as someone who got this when it first came out on console, I can say I really enjoyed it for what it is.
Once you get past the "escort" mission, the game really is great. The companions you get from other people are questionable, sure, but what they lack in immersive names they make up for in funny hats.
TLDR; "They're masterworks all, you can't go wrong."

My 2015's GOTY
Story/Lore/Quests:

Gameplay:
The gameplay is perfect. There is a fun stealth mechanic as well. Traps to look out for, hidden treasure or passage ways to be found. As for combat it is excellent. A lot of strategy to be at hand. Trying to assemble bottleneck's, your own trap's, mass of spells and ton's of variety to keep it interesting. Although sometimes the combat does feel taxing. Constantly pausing and unpausing but I don't mind it, just a note.
Graphics/Sound:
The graphics are perfect. Literally the best of any RPG with this flavor. The zone's are awesome to run around in and just look amazing. Spells look fantastic and combat has weight to it. It looks great and makes the big battles pure eye candy to watch. The sound as well is perfect. Amazing music, some of the best I have heard in awhile. It blend's in very well. With both of these so top notch for the game it really has a high immersion affect. Playing in the dark you just get sucked into this game.
Performance:
Runs perfect as anyone would expect. No FPS drops or crashes. I have not ran into any bugs as well. Although I am playing a month or so after the release date. In other words the game has 0 issues.
Replayability:
To much. Ton's of classes to play and choices to make. This game is packed with content.
Overall:
It really is my GOTY. Pillars was such a breath of fresh air in the lately stale market of gaming. This is Baldur's Gate brought back modern day the literal best way possible. I can't quit playing and I am yet to not enjoy myself as hours upon hours just pass by. GOTY.

Savage Lands offers a different approach on the succesful and thriving survival genre. It starts you off with the bare essentials such as basic clothing and tools. Using your wits but mainly your tools you must gather resources to fix up a shelter. Though before you can build a shelter that is not a Lean To you must create things like a blacksmith, crafting bench, and other useful things. This leads to a grind but that is my favorite part of the game. After that you start to venture farther into the island where you will fight skeletons, wolves, tiny tree creatures, and eventually the boss of the island who i believe is named Krull. With a wide amount of different structures, types/kinds of tools, and enemies you start to dive deeper into the other islands hungry for better loot. The lore notes you can also find scattered around hint on what has happened to the island and why it has come to be this way along with the blizzards make it so you are enthralled by the islands. Regarding the multiplayer i have played it a few times and i enjoyed it even better then i did the single player. This game also features a amazing scenery which i did not regard as highly as i should have. I was very confused when i got this game wondering what to do and how to do it. So i would like to thank Schack for not only giving me the game but also for teaching me how to play. I would recommend waiting to see if this game goes into further development but i believe that it is fine and playable in it's current starte. Note this is my opinion and others may view it differently.

Astroboy Edge of Time is based on Osamu Tezuka's Astro Boy anime. Thematically, the world is currently fighting for equal rights for robots and humans. However, the Deadcross Society, run by Deadcross is out to prevent equal rights for robots. I won't spoil the story for you so you can Google it for yourself. In this game, you play as a summoner, summoning units and fighting with cards.
Presentation-wise, the game is presented in a visual novel style with coloured characters speaking text on the left and right. Everything is presented with ultra lengthy English text with no way to fast forward.
As for gameplay, it is basically Hearthstone with 2 zones for each play, Guardian and Enforcer. The objective is to knock your opponent's hitpoints down to 0. The Guardian zone is where you place units to prevent direct damage to your hero. The Enforcer zone is where you place units that attack your opponent and their creature's.
There are 4 factions in the game, Red, Purple, Yellow and Blue. Red are the 9 King's, Purple are the Ministry of Science, Yellow are the Order of the Burning Feathers and Blue is the Gearwork Revolution.
Conclusion, I am not overtly interested due to the Pay To Win system and rarity creep. It might be better to just watch the anime instead. The quality of the game is similar to the Flash games on Kongregate.
NOTES : A collaboration between Tezuka Productions, Project Atom and Active Gaming Media.
1. Simple to Pick Up
Due to the similarities with Magic the Gathering and Hearthstone, it's easy to pick up.
2. Interactive Bits
Not fantastic but a good try. E.g. The professor in the shop winks if you click on him. Your base lights up with different things if you mouseover them.
3. Races
Demon, Human, H. Rocket, Machine
1. Pay To Win
100 Prisma for a basic pack. A 30-day subscription costs $28.99. 10 Packs cost $11.99.
2. Visual Novel Art Quality
While I am not against the visual art style, the art quality is very different compared to other Hearthstone clones such as Shadowverse.
a. Frenzy : 1 more attack if unit dies due to combat damage
b. Protective Halo : Prevents death if lethal once
c. Construct : Occurs when summoned
d. Flash : Can activate when summoned
e. Juggernaut : Hits Hero while attacking Guardians
3. The Extreme Similarity to Hearthstone
The gameplay mechanic is the same. The Guardian and Enforcer zones are basically defence and offence. You can find this mechanic in games like Infinity Wars. Certain abilities require the card to be played in a specific zone to gain the effect.
4. Money Grab Feeling
It feels like a money grab on the Osamu Tezuka heritage. In Japan, Osamu Tezuka is considered the anime "god" while Hayao Miyazaki is the "father" of anime. Hayao Miyazaki used to work under Osamu Tezuka until he left to strike out on his own.
5. Rarity Creep
In the game shop, you can buy Uncommon, Rare and Super Rare Cards. The prices range from $0.99(100 Prisma) to $5.99 (1000 Prisma) per card.
6. Ultra Lengthy Dialogue
Translation from Japanese to English will result in a longer text. TLDR.
7. Few Cards
There are too few cards to provide sufficient variety.

This game is genuinely enjoyable and a welcome surprise.
It is actually MUCH more generous in giving cards than it appears. You don't get a huge amount to start off but the regular booster seems to have a really good chance of containing higher rarity cards (I would recommend getting those and not buying the specific cards from the shop). On top of that the free login rewards are excellent. Every 7 days you get a golden booster pack which is guaranteed to contain five Rare or Super Rare cards (the top two rarities in the game). Combine that with draft mode, similar to Hearthstone arena mode, which also awards a golden pack if you get 5 wins and you can get a competitive deck together very quickly. Definitely not remotely P2W.
I enjoyed the story mode a lot. Even though the plot line isn't, shall we say, the most logical ever, the presentation of it is polished in addition to it giving decent rewards. I like it when CCG designers put effort in their single player mode and this game definitely does.
More importantly, the design of the game itself is solid. It's a tempo-based card game similar to Hearthstone but with more tactical depth and less RNG. It doesn't reinvent the wheel in terms of innovative design but from what I can tell from the first few hours it's decently balanced and reasonably strategic.
Finally, the visuals and soundtrack on this game are really quite good. Both do a great job at conveying a sort of futuristic, post-apocalyptic atmosphere and remain pleasing no matter how long you play the game for.
The only thing it's lacking at the moment is players, possibly due to a number of blatantly unfair reviews the game has been getting. This really is a lot better than most free-to-play CCGs on Steam right now and deserves at least a positive recommendation.

TL; DR - Really good card game with tons of possibilities. Takes place in a really cool world. Art and music by respected cast of Japanese talents. It's okay if you don't know about the wild genius of Osamu Tezuka. Devs are VERY on top of bug fixes so far.
Long: I haven't really played any of the Hearthstone games or their clones. I played Magic when I was younger and found the new school to be too simplistic. This game is definitely new school (ie. the abilities rarely take more than one sentence to explain), but I'm a HUGE fan of Osamu Tezuka and had no choice but to check it out. If you ever enjoyed a manga or anime, you have him to thank. It's often said "Why doesn't the rest of the world read comics as ubiquitously as people of all ages in Japan? Because the rest of the world didn't have Tezuka.". I'll stop nerding out about him now though, and say that you don't need to know anything about him to appreciate this scene. They've cobbled together his library of work into this weird world and it just results in a crazy place where you can get a little of everything. You want robot dragons or magic ninjas? Cool. They all live here.
The game is really good and you can already see numerous directions that you can take the four factions. The in game currency is really simple. The likelihood of finding super rare cards in a pack is apparently relatively high too.
The soundtrack is kindof a big deal. It was done by Akira Yamaoka (of Silent Hill fame) using old analogue synths. I hafta admit that I was a little disappointed by the end product, but really just as a matter of taste. It has an 80's cyber-punk-cheese thing going for it that'll appeal to many, just not me..
This game was clearly well funded on the Japanese end and has a lot of relevant Japanese artists doing the card art. For many, getting to do Tezuka characters is kindof a big deal. So, the result is a lot of great card art.
The story is a little long-winded when it's justifying random battle #12 or whatever, but I think they have a larger plot in mind that could play out well.
Also, it's free so just go get it.

"State of Decay" is the love letter to the zombie genre zed enthusiats have been waiting for.  The experiences I've had in SoD are comparable to those I've had in L4D (and, no, I'm not talking multiplayer fun for all).  It's a game that really makes you think about your next move, and keeps you mindful of the stock of ammo, food, medicine, building materials and fuel you have.  Everything you do in SoD potentially has a consequence (which is why I feel some people don't like this game- they don't like their choices not working out positively).  I've seen some people complain about how the game is "persistent" when you're not playing, but all that does is requires a little thought before you log off.  Check to see what type of stock you're short on, and go and get it.  Also, see if there is any home facilities you can upgrade, and cook a big meal to keep morale/stamina high.  The combat is pretty sweet, as well.  Once you understand the mechanics, you'll be dodging and countering attacks in no time.  Also worth noting is the "George Romero Mod" that's available.  It let's you further shape the apocalypse you want to endure.  I have it set to no Special Infected, Slow zombies that attack with tenacity, and believe me- it's amazing.  I've never had a zombie game where the zombies were the ONLY serious threat, and with that mod, every encounter with a horde could potentially be life/death.  Some people are jaded over the multiplayer aspect, and I would love to enjoy this game with a friend, but honestly, it's ridiculous to me that some people would dismiss this game based on that simple fact.  I think people tend to forget the Undead Labs is an Indie Company and this game is essentially just an XBLA game.  And with those two factors in mind, you really DO get your moneys worth- I've played this game more than any other XBLA title I've ever purchased.  Sometimes while playing it's hard to even believe it's just an Arcade title.
Overall: 10/10.  If you love zombies, and don't mind seeing your choices ♥♥♥♥ everything up, this is the game for you!

Probably the better of the zombie apocalypse game out there, that mixes strategy with combat, though it doesn't excel at both, but at a sufficient level where it's fun. The controls will probably♥♥♥♥♥♥you off, since it was a port from the xbox 360. For example, sometimes your movement controls don't register so you can't move. Also this game takes the award for the worst handling of cars. You will crash a lot, and not even on purpose. While driving, you have 3 ways to go; straight, which is holding W, completely right, D, or completely left, A.  Even if you lightly tap D, you will still make a hard right, and probably fly off the road. Going back to movement controls, since sometimes your wasd won't register, you may find your character swinging their weapon away at the air, while zombies approach him from behind, simply because the controls refuse to let you swing in any direction. Maybe there was a fly that really bothered your character, who knows.
For a survival game, the difficulty varies a lot. If you ever played S.T.A.L.K.E.R on the hardest difficulty and did well, this game may be a cake walk for you, since you obviously have the patience to take things slow and plan ahead. State of Decay can range from pretty simple, to ridiculously hard. If you go the stealth route, like in S.T.A.L.K.E.R, the game may can play out easier. If you prefer more of a combat arcade style, then prepare for endless amounts of zombies running to your location from the noise, which seems fun, but as in S.T.A.L.K.E.R, dealing with even three enemies at once can be really dangerous. But the main point of using stealth or combat is the same: Find supplies. You'll have to make trips to each building, searching for what it offers: Food, Ammo, Medicine, or Building Materials. Interesting concept, but tedious after a while since you can only carry 1 bag at a time, though I guess it is a "Survival" game, so it tries to get close to how life would really be.
Graphics, sound, and voice overs are fine. Music is pretty good. Voices are ok, repetitive but ok. Graphics are sufficient, blood and gore, can't mess that up. Though the bugs in the game become obvious pretty early. Sometimes zombies glitch through walls, or glitch through the ground, only there heads sliding around on the floor. Sometimes zombies will grab you in mid air, or out of reach as they glitch over to you. None of them too game breaking, annoying and stupid, but it happens once in a while. Though the worst is sometimes quests don't trigger, rendering them impossible to complete. It's rare, but it can occur since it happened to me once.
Despite some mishaps, I still find myself absorbed into the game. The game keeps going on without you, so even when you log off and go to sleep in real life. You can wake up and find out what happened to your group of survivors while you were away. Sometimes they are sick, sometimes they gathered more supplies, sometimes they can even commit suicide while you were away. All of this kind of keeps the game going, the unexpected is always around the corner. Each character has a story to tell. You start to bond with them, and when one of them dies, it's not that simple "Oh lost a guy", It's "Damn, that guy was our expert shooter, how can I defend against the hordes now?" So you keep gathering supplies, helping out other survivors, clearing the infestations, recruiting people, and before you know it, you've been playing the game for over 5 hours. I have to honestly say, so far this game hits the top survival games I've played (S.T.A.L.K.E.R still remains number one for me).
So, to sum up, the game has it's problems, but more than makes up for it. If your a zombie fan, you'll probably like this game as a chance to really see how well you'd do in a real apocalypse. Would you help out fellow survivors, doing errands for them keeping them safe in your base? Or ignore all plees for help, only looking out for you and your small group of friends, staying alive and not taking the risk. For people who like hack and slash fast paced games, this may not hit the spot, but its a fun alternative none the less.

Unique stories from the Nemesis system.
I knew a guy. Norsko. 'The Rat', they called him. Rats run, but not Norsko. No, Norsko was a fighter. A good one.
First Uruk to send me to the grave, he was. I was young and foolish, testing my strength against whoever I could find. Then he appears, a name. The first one I've faced. Adrenaline pumping, I take him on. He's good, but I can match him. But then my inexperience starts to show. I'm surrounded. More captains show up. I thought I was invincible. Norsko showed me I was wrong.
A lot of promotions were handed out that day. Ranks changed hands. It's funny how a body can carry more weight when dead. Norsko got the brunt of the appraise and applause. He took a step forward, gloating the whole time. I didn't like that. At all.
I rose from the dead, blood boiling. I wanted revenge so badly. I hunted Norsko down and tried to kill him. Instead I found out how much revenge can cost.
I was slowly learning that Norsko got stronger everytime he killed me. More powerful in more than just rank. My determination to kill him never wavered and eventually I got my wish. It took time, another captain getting a lucky shot in, a lot of orc corpses and a few of my own but I did it. His power level was 9 and I made sure he never saw double digits first-hand. Norsko was no more.
Or so I thought.
Somehow, he didn't die. I was running free sometime later, already forgotten him when he attacked me. Suprise and shock were the brothers by my side as I read that dreaded name. I didn't understand it. It must be a error. So I decided to debug it and once again teach Norsko how much better off he was when his head departed his shoulders.
But it didn't end. He appeared again sometime after that. He was more powerful and had a poisoned mace. His presence certainly felt like poison. And his taunts always beat themselves into my skull. Norsko would not die, even when I killed him. This time he was better of us. I ran. Since then I could only watch as he lived on, bearing the scars of our history as his power increased. One day, there she stood. Mightiest of the captains yet not even a warchief. Power level 20.
Skirmish after skirmish and we learned to stop killing each other; he couldn't manage it and I didn't want to. Truth be told, I was proud of him. We'd both made it as far as we had by killing each other. If there was a chance that we could break the cycle, killing Norsko for good, it would wait. Norsko was an enemy worth fighting. A rival to wrestle with. A foe to give battle purpose. He was my nemesis.
It was sadly not to last. I had only started killing warchiefs when it happened. Norsko was my dear Ratbag the Coward's bodyguard so there was even some tactical worth in keeping him alive at this point. Naturally it was entirely my concern when a duel was struck up between him and some level 8 trash. I forget the whelp's name as he was not even worth remembering. We shall call him Morgul. I do recall that he was known as 'Map Bearer'.
I decided to take part in watching this bloodbath. Perhaps I shouldn't have. We'd always cursed each other, but I never wanted this. I expected Norsko to triumph easily, as he should. He wasn't unstoppable, as I knew firsthand, but there was no enemy who'd made the progress he had. It should have gone to him. But life isn't fair.
The poisoned mace was a pretty thing, but when you aren't as fast as a Ranger, it's sadly ineffective against a shield and trident. As I watched I realised that Norsko was losing. At once I felt a need to protect my personal villain from an ungainly death. I resolved to step in and save his life if he should reach critical levels. It was a decision made too late and too indecisively. Even as I steeled myself to interfere, Morgul jabbed with such ferocity that he wiped Norsko's health out from over the halfway point.
In one single blow, Norsko was gone. For good this time. His position wouldn't be redeemed through his animated corpse it would be stolen by this 'Morgul Map Bearer' who I had known for all of two missions. It was unjust. It was unworthy. I should have been the one to kill him. It should have been a fight with grandeur and closure. It should have been our personal showdown after all we'd been through where I finally put him in his place and proved to him that we were no longer equals and we never would be again.
But that right was lost in this single accidental moment of weakness. It would not be unpaid for.
I leapt from my perch and in the single push of a button, in a single flash of my blade, I cut Morgul Map Bearer's throat, killing him at once. It wasn't fair to have his rightful victory snatched from him, but after watching an unknown fool kill my longtime nemesis I was in no mood to discuss injustice. As his life slipped away I whispered to him: "Norsko would never have fallen to that." It's true. He was immune to stealth.
I looked down upon the miserable faces of the two dead Uruk who had come here to contest each other, willing to take on the risk of death, even if it meant no longer fighting the people they truly hated and I realised, as their followers fled the scene and as I stood there in the middle of it all, collecting their final runes to remember them by, nobody was happy. Nobody left that day with a warm heart and a smiling face.
Was it worth it? Should I have done that?
I may never make up my mind on any of it save for one detail. Nobody in all of Mordor - in all of Middle Earth - will ever match the glory of my one true nemesis.
Farewell, Norsko the Rat.

We rented this game from the video store to try it out, and we liked it well enough to buy one. I thoroughly enjoy this game in spite of some flaws in the animation. Maybe that's because my criterion for a good game is that it should challenge my reasoning skills. This game definitely does that!
Although "Chantelise" is rated "6 years and older" in terms of content (from the G-rated movie), it's a difficult game that might frustrate some children, and will definitely challenge adults. It has five "worlds" with 3 levels each (that's 15 levels in all). So far, I've only gotten to Level 4 (where the Bird gobbles me up every time!) Each time I play, however, I discover new tricks and features that I missed before.
The real trick in this game is not bashing badongo's at breakneck speed, it's figuring out the best order to collect the various items. True, Elise's Red Berries are very hard to aim and you need several throws to do much good. They're meant to be that way, because they're his least powerful weapon. But find that green Homing Berry, and your aiming problems are solved, because it follows the target like a smart bomb! Also, I didn't find Chante's harvester on Level 1 until I had played for several hours -- but once I did, my whole strategy changed the next time around. And I'm sure it will change again, once I find whatever it is I need to get past that darned Bird!
I give this game a 0/10 though, because its gaaaay af.

Reminds me a one of the Japanese action RPG from PS1. We don't see this often enough, and that's a shame.
Now, indeed this game is bit hard to control if you are not use to it, but you can map it from game folder. Go to local game folder, open Steam\Steamapps\common\Chantelise and you can configure the control from there.
I used this mapping- ←→↑↓for movement, A for attack, S for Jump, D for dash, F for lock-on, left Shift and space for camera angle. Trust me, this works like charm.
Now on to the game. I loved it. I beat it, and I still play it from time to time. Stroyline isn't much deep and straight forward, but it's charming and easy to play. English translation is bit cheesy though- I played it on Japanese because... I am. It's almost like a mixture of Xenogears, Mario, and Zelda. Fun beat'em up, less puzzle.
Only downside that I can think about is that the dungeon is very simple and only one-way direction. All you have to do is to defeat all enemies and unlock the gate, rinse and repeat. The boss battle is more fun. You have to figureout the pattern of the movement, and find the weakpoint. This part tends to be more like Zelda.
You will also unlock few more things, like having magic on your sword. Charge attack will release the magic with several different ability, and I thought that was fun.
Anyway, I would recommend this game, especially if you like doujin games. You won't be dissappointed.

This game was released in 2006 by EasyGameStation at the Comiket in Japan. The same group that made Recettear An Item Shop's Tale. It was translated and brought to Steam by Carpe Fulgur in 2011.
In this game you play a little anime girl with her fairy sidekick sister. You adventure through dungeons, defeating enemies with sword and magic attacks. Of course this reminds you of Zelda and it plays a bit like one. It focuses much more on combat though, akin to a Ys-type of game. The game features a blend of 2D sprites in a 3D world, which works surprisingly well. I had some issues with aiming in the beginning, but that worked itself out after a while.
The magic system is the central part of the gameplay. You use different colored gems to cast fire, water, wind and earth spells. These gems are used in the order you pick them up from the ground, but when you hold the cast button longer you use up to three gems at once. This way various different colored gems can be combined and produce different spells. This make for quite the deep system and keeps the combat interesting. ♥♥♥♥ earth though. Those gems are worthless.
There are no levels, so you only improve through your items. This makes the game faster and removes the grind you have in typical JRPGs. Upon death a Game Over screen pops up, but you just respawn at the town, which makes dying forgiving. That is needed though, because you will die a lot.
I actually had a lot of fun with the story, especially the characters. I don't know if it is thanks to the translation or source, but there are some really funny lines in there. I recommend this game, if you like some oldschool dungeoning.

I used to play this game for hours on console, and now playing it on PC, it's still so easy to see why I fell in love with this game. First, here's pros/cons:
Pros:
+ Unique battle system (reminiscent of Shadow of the Colossus at times, hack & slash RPG at other times)
+ Variety of classes/skills for custom builds
+ Spells in the game look & feel AMAZING when you're using them
+ Character customization (not only can you customize your own character, but you can also customize your companion).
+ Solid voice acting (*see cons list for 2 comments on this)
+ Environments look pretty good (it's a screenshot-worthy game at times)
+ Enemy variety is much better than most RPGs
+ Great replay value (end-game changes in NG+)
+ DLC that can be extremely hard, depending on your skill/character levels. Provides a good reason to keep leveling.
+ Small choices in the game can lead to consequences down the road (i.e. You can keep (or pay an NPC to dupe) items instead of turning in quests, but if that item is missing/magical (NPC dupes don't have magical properties), then certain cutscenes can trigger where if a character has that quest item, you'd save a ton of time/get special items.
Neutral:
Character models are really hit and miss. Some look great, others are pretty bad (when talking/showing emotions)
Soundtrack, for me, is also hit or miss. Some tracks are A+, others are forgettable.
Some dungeons feel like they go on ENTIRELY too long. (These past two points are subjective, I know)
The fast travel system is complete bull-crap at times. Other times it's not half bad. All in all, I put this in neutral.
A lot of quests can be completely skipped, especially if you don't go hunting for them at weird times. Without these, some characters just disappear and you don't know why, or show up in weird places without a backstory.
Cons:
- *A ton of lines for your companions (you make one & choose two others, for a party of 4) are all recycled entirely too much. I'm talking like "I'm sworn to carry your burdens"-level. (
)
- *One or two characters were supposed to have an accent, and you can tell that the VA forced it. It's not immersion-breaking, but whoever did QC on it shouldn't have let it pass.
- The game is no stranger to the idea of re-using story dungeons for side quests.
- The game uses a point-based romance system to decide who you "end up with" at the end (unless you acquire a certain item through a side quest). Not being careful toward the end of the game can make your character end up with a certain NPC who gives you a metric ton of quests 2/3 of the way through the game, as completing quests gives huge point boosts.
- While the story is fantastic, the writing toward the end is slightly melodramatic and convoluted. The payout is totally worth it, I just think it could use some touch-ups or maybe make a few silent scenes better animated to match their emotions.
- There's a gifting system that does literally nothing, unless you give the same character 40 billion copies of the same thing, and even then the impact is so small that if you just so much as un-sheath your weapon in front of them, those 40 billion copies are negated.
- It suffers from a Skyrim complex (i.e. "Oh, I'm dying." *Opens up menu and consumes 5 health items*). Some like this style, but I prefer there to at least be some sort of potion-drinking animation so I at least don't feel like 54 cheese wheels can resurrect the almost-dead.
-------------
Overall, I give the game a solid 8.5/10.
-------------
It's definitely not perfect, but it's a lot better than most RPG games out there. Not only can you climb enemies, but many bosses are so much larger-than-life, that you'll need to if you want to have any hope of defeating them.
If you want to play a ranged/magic-based character, this game is fantastic for that, too. You can even combine them and use a magic archer, who summons arrows out of thin air. Not a lot of games allow that. And when it comes to spells, summoning a lightning bolt and using it as whip, or even summoning a tornado--the visual effects on spells in this game are stunning and very well animated.
The story-line often takes work to find, as a lot of quests are buried or only available during a very short time (one character's personal quest is unavailable until you complete one main quest mission, and is then unavailable after you accept the very next main quest mission. Meaning if you don't turn the first quest in, leave, and find the NPC, the quest is just GONE. And considering how important that quest is to knowing why in the world she can just show up later, it can be pretty confusing if you don't play it.)
But when you DO find the story, it's very well written and quite compelling. There are a few animated cutscenes that aren't the most polished, but for a game that came out when it did, and how much customization there is, I can't really complain, especially when the environment looks like it does. This game aims for "gritty, dark fantasy" at times, and "magical, high-fantasy" at other times, and it's always right on the nose.
Again, 8.5/10. It's not perfect, but it's far better than others give it credit for. I consider this the hidden gem of 2012. While others were still exploring Skyrim, I was playing this, and I don't regret it.

TLDR; "They're masterworks all, you can't go wrong."

Hylics is weird. Really weird. Its creator, Mason Lindroth, has described it as "a recreational program with light JRPG elements" instead of a "video game", and that's pretty accurate. The joy of Hylics doesn't lie so much within its turn-based battles (which I still find quite fun) as much as it does within simply experiencing the various corners of the absolutely absurd world that Lindroth has created here. It's stunningly beautiful even as it eludes comprehension. I could give details but you owe it to yourself to jump in and see for yourself. If playing alongside friends, the game will be a hilarious misadventure in random-text generation. If played alone, it  will be a stunningly artistic experience. I absolutely love it. For $3, give it a shot.

Hylics is an experience that I recommend to anyone with entirely too much three bucks and entirely not enough good times. It's an experience that doesn't last long, but doesn't overstay its welcome that way.

I would not currently recommend this game. I was trying to support the game. I was trying to like it. I've finally lost my patience. Yes, the developers are very active and talk with the  community, but as a player, I am just not having fun with the game and don't want to play it anymore. I also don't like the way the game is turning out, so I'm out.
1. Very small community. You will spend most of your time looking for a match. You won't get to play at all unless you are really dedicated and are ready to wait for 20+ minutes at a time. I have definitely spent more than 1 session waiting 17+ hours for a match never to find one. I've definitely lost my patience. If it's more than 10 seconds, I'm logging.
2. The new cards that I've seen so far for the upcoming expansion are very RNG heavy. This is looking like it is going down the exact same path as Hearthstone. No thanks.
3. All of their events have been for their draft mode. I hate draft. I prefer constructed. Have fun with RNG heavy gambling draft mode.
Going back to good card games like Shardbound, Eternal, and Gwent. I'm done wasting my time on this.
Also, if you think that this is just a cash grab, you'd be wrong. This started out as an indie kickstarter by a very passionate team. I'd just rather play a game to have fun. This game has been a headache since I installed it.
My background:
I was the first person to Master Rank in ranked mode.
I have a 98% win rate with a single loss in ranked.
I have every card in the game minus a promo card and cards from the upcoming expansion.
I've had a 30 win streak in draft mode several times.
My playtime hours on this game speaks for itself. I definitely gave this game a chance and I definitely learned the meta and how to build good draft decks. Note that most of my playtime took place between June 19th to June 26th. After that I'd just login to the game for a minute or so to see if I could find a match and then eventually I more or less just stopped logging in.
